intended_object: The canonical group unitaries u_k (k ∈ K) of the group-measure-space crossed product L^∞(Ω) ⋊ K, acting on ℓ²(K, L²(Ω)) ≅ L²(Ω) ⊗ ℓ²(K) by (u_k ξ)(h) = σ_k(ξ(k⁻¹h)), where σ_k f = f ∘ α_{k⁻¹}. Inferred from the docstring, the paper reference (§3) and the use in crossedGeneratorSet/crossedProductModel.
explanation: The body composes reindexing by left multiplication by k (ξ ↦ (h ↦ ξ(k⁻¹h)), the left regular representation λ_k) with the fiberwise Koopman unitary σ_k f = f ∘ action(k⁻¹). This gives (u_k ξ)(h) = σ_k(ξ(k⁻¹h)), which the rfl lemma crossedGroupUnitary_apply confirms. Composing the actions shows σ_kσ_l = σ_{kl}, so u_k u_l = u_{kl}. Together with the multipliers π(f)ξ(h) = f·ξ(h) defined in the same file, the covariance relation u_k π(f) u_k* = π(σ_k f) holds. On the vacuum δ_1 ⊗ 1 the vector state gives the standard trace (∫f if k = 1, else 0). This is the standard σ ⊗ λ picture of the crossed product, unitarily equivalent to the other common picture (π(f)ξ(h) = σ_{h⁻¹}(f)ξ(h) with u_k = λ_k). K carries no topology, so it is treated as discrete, which is the natural setting. The unitary itself uses only that the action preserves the measure; the extra structure on Ω (an additive group with a Haar probability measure) comes from the library's HaarProbabilityAction, which fits the paper's Connes-rigidity setting, and this definition is that model's own group unitary. Mathlib has no crossed-product von Neumann algebra construction to compare against.
